To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probability of a word being the next word in the text is predictive of the time spent fixating on it and the location of the first fixation on the word.

the forward and backward transitional probability measures are predictive of first fixation duration and gaze duration in reading; that the measures account equally well for function and content words; and that the measures predict initial fixation position.

the probability that a word will be preceded by another word (forward) is positively correlated with fixation time, the probability that a target word will be followed by another (backward) is also positively correlated with fixation times, and the initial fixation position is positively correlated with the forward transitional probability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of low-level, statistical, lexical information in reading.
the role of low-level, probabilistic information in the control of eye movements during reading.
the role of low-level predictive processes in the control of eye movements during reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transitional probabilities are a useful predictor of low-level eye movement behaviour, but that they are only one of several predictors.
transitional probabilities do influence eye movements in reading.
transitional probabilities do have a small effect on eye movements during reading, and that they do so in a manner consistent with the predictions of the E-Z Reader model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

transitional probability is a low-level predictive cue that is able to influence the eye movements of skilled readers, but that its influence is relatively small and is overshadowed by the effects of other, higher-level factors.
the influence of transitional probability in reading is a low-level effect that operates in parallel with higher-level processes.
the influence of transitional probability is pervasive and that the influence is similar in both content and function words.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transitional probability is an important factor in the control of reading behaviour.
transitional probability can be used to predict low-level reading behaviour.
the influence of transitional probability on reading behaviour is not limited to the processing of function words, but is a more general phenomenon.
